title: Multiclass classification: what its pitfalls cost on its replica
question: On the Multiclass classification replica, how much better does a wrong split or a kept leak make the score look?
setup_summary: 3 seeds of the multiclass replica; 20% held out; histogram gradient boosting with default settings; accuracy; right split: the latest rows by time.

claims.statement: On the Multiclass classification replica, a random split instead of the latest rows by time showed no difference beyond the spread of 3 seeds (mean 0.0432, 95% interval -0.0208 to 0.1073).
limitations: Invented replica data with its traps planted, one model family with default settings: the size of the effect on a real table differs; the direction is what the replica shows.

No difference measured on this replica: it plants no effect of this kind (no drift over time), which says nothing about a real table, where a random split is still the wrong one for a time-ordered problem.

claims.statement: On the Multiclass classification replica, the planted leak kept in makes the accuracy look better by 0.4341 on average over 3 seeds (95% interval 0.3591 to 0.5091).
limitations: Invented replica data with its traps planted, one model family with default settings: the size of the effect on a real table differs; the direction is what the replica shows.
